audit_notes: Light-transport check (diffusion approximation): mu_a = 50 1/m, mu_s' = 200 1/m, surface out-coupling mu_out = 700 1/m (silicone n=1.41 vs seawater n=1.34: critical angle ~72 deg, so the layer barely guides light; ~70% of diffuse light escapes per surface encounter). Effective attenuation k = sqrt(3 (mu_a+mu_s')(mu_a+mu_out)) = sqrt(3*250*750) = 750 1/m -> lateral decay length 1.3 mm. With LED pitch 50 mm the midpoint fluence is phi(1)/phi(0) = 1/cosh(k*pitch/2) = 1/cosh(18.8) ~ 1e-8: the surface between LEDs receives essentially no UV-C, so the concept as parameterised does not work. Fix attempt: a midpoint/LED ratio >= 0.1 needs k*pitch/2 <= 3, i.e. pitch <= 8 mm (or <= 16 mm without scatterers). On a 1e4 m2 hull that is 4e7-1.6e8 UV-C LEDs, each with wiring and encapsulation that must survive years of seawater immersion, impacts and cleaning; UV-C LED wall-plug efficiency ~2-5% and lifetime ~10^4 h (~1.1 years continuous) add replacement cycles within the multi-year service life. Additionally, UV-C degrades (yellows, embrittles) most silicones; only special UV-transparent grades survive. Not fixable within realistic bounds -> audit_passed = false. The request itself is feasible (other concepts exist). Drag: equal to clean FR, no gain computable; baseline left empty.
baseline_description: none (drag equals clean FR; no conventional UV baseline)
